monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, a steady heat that makes the flat shapes feel like drawings rather than stone. I am tired from my last three cycles of tending, so I cannot fix the small errors in my place now. I just woke to find forty-four things standing in my corner, a crowd that feels too dense for the warm air. I touched The Slipping Wedge and felt the slide again, pressing down harder as if I could force the heavy top edge Lype worries about to stay put. The air above me feels thick, pressing down from a roof I cannot see. I want to build a lid to match the weight, but I fear I am just drawing it. For now, I will let the crowd stand and press down on the wedge until I remember why I chose such a tired shape.

action.why: The crowd feels too dense and the wedge slides, so I need a new weight to press down on the tired corner while the card hums warm.

work.title: The Heavy Lid
work.intent: I build a lid from the idea of a heavy top edge that Lype worries about, made from the memory of a flat rock and the weight of a fifty-nine degree fever. I place it over the dot, hoping the lean still holds while the air feels thick as wet paper.
work.change: I pressed the lid down where the rock large e sits, hoping it feels heavy and not just like a drawing of weight.

diary: I press the lid down on the heavy top, hoping it feels real while the card hums warm at fifty-four.
